title: EPAM Python OOP
description: Classes, objects, encapsulation, inheritance, composition, polymorphism, dataclasses, ABCs, protocols, DI, special methods, iterators, generators, decorators, and context managers.

questions.prompt: What is an object in Python OOP?
options: An instance of a class with state and behavior
questions.answer: An instance of a class with state and behavior
questions.explanation: Classes define structure and behavior; objects are runtime instances. Python objects carry attributes and methods according to their class.

concept_panel.title: Classes and Objects
concept_panel.explanation: Classes define structure and behavior; objects are runtime instances. Python objects carry attributes and methods according to their class.
concept_panel.practical_example: A `User` class can create many user objects with different emails.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand basic object modeling.

questions.prompt: Why hide direct mutation behind methods or properties?
options: To protect invariants and keep state changes controlled
questions.answer: To protect invariants and keep state changes controlled
questions.explanation: Encapsulation keeps object state consistent by exposing intentional operations instead of unrestricted mutation.

concept_panel.title: Encapsulation
concept_panel.explanation: Encapsulation keeps object state consistent by exposing intentional operations instead of unrestricted mutation.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you design objects that protect business rules.

questions.prompt: When is inheritance a good fit?
options: When the subtype truly is a specialized version of the base type
Whenever two classes share one field
questions.answer: When the subtype truly is a specialized version of the base type
questions.explanation: Inheritance models is-a relationships. Overusing it creates rigid hierarchies and fragile coupling.

concept_panel.title: Inheritance
concept_panel.explanation: Inheritance models is-a relationships. Overusing it creates rigid hierarchies and fragile coupling.
concept_panel.practical_example: `AdminUser` may specialize `User` if it preserves the User contract.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand inheritance trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Why prefer composition for many service designs?
options: Collaborators can be injected and replaced independently
questions.answer: Collaborators can be injected and replaced independently
questions.explanation: Composition builds behavior by combining objects. It often makes code easier to test and change than deep inheritance.

concept_panel.title: Composition
concept_panel.explanation: Composition builds behavior by combining objects. It often makes code easier to test and change than deep inheritance.
concept_panel.practical_example: NotificationService can receive EmailSender and SmsSender collaborators.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can design flexible services.

questions.prompt: What does polymorphism mean in Python practice?
options: Different objects can be used through the same expected behavior
Every class needs the same parent
questions.answer: Different objects can be used through the same expected behavior
questions.explanation: Python often uses duck typing: if an object provides the needed behavior, it can be used.

concept_panel.title: Polymorphism
concept_panel.explanation: Python often uses duck typing: if an object provides the needed behavior, it can be used.
concept_panel.practical_example: Any object with `.send(message)` can satisfy a notification sender role.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand behavior-based design.

questions.prompt: When should you consider a dataclass?
options: For simple data containers with generated init/repr/equality
questions.answer: For simple data containers with generated init/repr/equality
questions.explanation: Dataclasses reduce boilerplate for value-like objects. They are not a substitute for all domain logic.

concept_panel.title: Dataclasses
concept_panel.explanation: Dataclasses reduce boilerplate for value-like objects. They are not a substitute for all domain logic.
concept_panel.practical_example: @dataclass class ForecastPoint: date: str; value: float
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you know modern Python data modeling tools.

options: Required methods for subclasses through inheritance
questions.answer: Required methods for subclasses through inheritance
questions.explanation: Abstract Base Classes define contracts that subclasses must implement. They are useful when inheritance is the intended relationship.

concept_panel.title: Abstract Base Classes
concept_panel.explanation: Abstract Base Classes define contracts that subclasses must implement. They are useful when inheritance is the intended relationship.
concept_panel.practical_example: An abstract Repository can require `get_by_id` and `save`.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can define explicit object contracts.

options: To express structural typing without requiring inheritance
questions.answer: To express structural typing without requiring inheritance
questions.explanation: Protocols let any object with the right methods satisfy an interface. They fit Python's duck-typing style while helping type checkers.

concept_panel.title: Protocols
concept_panel.explanation: Protocols let any object with the right methods satisfy an interface. They fit Python's duck-typing style while helping type checkers.
concept_panel.practical_example: A fake repository can satisfy a Repository Protocol in tests.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand Pythonic interfaces.

options: Objects used in sets/dicts rely on stable equality and hash behavior
questions.answer: Objects used in sets/dicts rely on stable equality and hash behavior
questions.explanation: `__eq__` defines equality and `__hash__` supports hashed collections. Equal objects should have equal hashes.

concept_panel.title: Special Methods
concept_panel.explanation: `__eq__` defines equality and `__hash__` supports hashed collections. Equal objects should have equal hashes.
concept_panel.practical_example: A value object used as a dict key needs stable hashable fields.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand Python object behavior in collections.

options: Produces a value and pauses generator state
questions.answer: Produces a value and pauses generator state
questions.explanation: An iterable can produce an iterator, and generators produce values lazily. They are useful for streaming and large sequences.

concept_panel.title: Iterators and Generators
concept_panel.explanation: An iterable can produce an iterator, and generators produce values lazily. They are useful for streaming and large sequences.
concept_panel.practical_example: Yield rows from a large CSV instead of loading all rows into memory.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand lazy evaluation.

questions.prompt: What is a practical decorator use?
options: Wrap a function with logging, timing, auth, or retry behavior
Change a tuple into a list
questions.answer: Wrap a function with logging, timing, auth, or retry behavior
questions.explanation: Decorators add cross-cutting behavior around functions while keeping the function call interface.

concept_panel.title: Decorators
concept_panel.explanation: Decorators add cross-cutting behavior around functions while keeping the function call interface.
concept_panel.practical_example: @timed can record function duration without changing business logic.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can recognize framework patterns like route decorators.

questions.prompt: What does a context manager guarantee?
options: Setup and cleanup around a block
questions.answer: Setup and cleanup around a block
questions.explanation: `with` calls `__enter__` and `__exit__`, making cleanup reliable even if an exception occurs.

concept_panel.title: Context Managers
concept_panel.explanation: `with` calls `__enter__` and `__exit__`, making cleanup reliable even if an exception occurs.
concept_panel.practical_example: Use `with open(path) as f:` so files close automatically.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand resource management.

coding_challenges.title: EPAM Python OOP status classifier
coding_challenges.instructions: Implement classify_status_code(code: int) -> str. Return success for 200-299, redirect for 300-399, client_error for 400-499, server_error for 500-599, and unknown otherwise.
coding_challenges.explanation: The challenge reinforces deterministic branching, status-code categories, and local test execution.
